rendered: The document does not report that prestraining lowered the Li-ion diffusion coefficient. It reports the opposite: prestraining increased it. In the strained state the diffusion coefficient is observed to increase, by a factor of about[1] 2.5-times[2] compared with the unstrained state. The abstract gives the same result: the diffusion coefficient of lithium ions rises by up to[3] 2.5-times[4] with elastic prestrains of <2%[5] imposed on the V2O5. The stated reasoning is geometric. An out-of-plane compressive strain produces a net positive volume change in the film, because it gives in-plane tensile strains that increase the total volume of the crystal. The authors then suggest that the increase in diffusion coefficient could be due to a reduction of ion migration barriers, which can be achieved through imposed mechanical strains.[6][7]
